text: The service uses one login for schema rwb_agent, named by the P10 database story; the story calls it "the rwb-agent login (DP-02)" and the chart and the run reference it as a secret, never as a literal.
why: No source names the login of the service, but one schema and one login per service is the rule of Arch v5 slide 41 and DP-02, and the release cannot be rendered without a reference.
read: Arch v5 slides 20 and 41; Template and Rules §R4 and DP-02; RWB-P10-E1058-CON
applied_in: RWB-P10-TE013-APP section 3 and 10; RWB-P10-TE013-CON section 10; RWB-P10-TE013-OPS AC5 and section 10
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the ACE database administrator
impact: Only the name of the secret; no behaviour changes when it is agreed.

text: The run-step operation is served as POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-steps; the path below the base is fixed by RWB-P10-TE013-CON because the sources name only GET /agent-runs/{id} and the legacy Java interface AgentStepClient.runStep.
why: The legacy key publishes an interface and no HTTP operation, and the target needs one operation to replace it; the path is a contract choice and not a business value.
read: Legacy section 12; Arch v5 slide 16; TSD P10 v2 T-A.1; DP-11, DP-13, DP-20
applied_in: RWB-P10-TE013-APP section 12.1; RWB-P10-TE013-CON section 12.1; RWB-P10-TE013-OPS section 12.1
confirm: Solution architect and the calling services of wave 1
impact: One path in one contract; a later rename is an additive change with a new version.

text: The orchestrator call and the Enterprise AI endpoint INT-23 stay inside the agent platform of RWB-P10-E1058-APP, so the client story, the contract and the deployment add no dependency of their own for them.
why: Arch v5 slide 16 puts the tool gateway and the model call inside rwb-agent and names the endpoint as the service's only outside call; the client reaches the orchestrator and never the model.
read: Arch v5 slide 16; TSD P10 v2 T5.1; RWB-P10-E1058-CON
impact: No dependency row and no contract element for INT-23 in this key.

text: A step that falls back without producing an agent run publishes rwb.agent.AgentStepFallback.v1 on rwb.agent.events.v1, because only AgentRunCompleted is catalogued and a fallback with no run would otherwise leave no fact on the topic.
why: Arch v5 slide 43 catalogues EV-28 alone on the agent topic; the legacy story records a NO_POLICY and an OFF fallback with no agent run, and the fallback rate cannot be counted from the runs alone.
read: Arch v5 slide 43; legacy AC5 and AC8; DP-09, DP-14
applied_in: RWB-P10-TE013-APP section 12.3; RWB-P10-TE013-CON AC4 and section 12.3
confirm: Data steward and the owner of the event catalogue
impact: One added event on the service's own topic, with no personal data and no consumer outside Arch v5 slide 43.

text: LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-AGENT-RUN and LOV-CONFIG-STATUS are read from the rwb-case reference-data contract; an empty or unreachable list stops the step and no default list is used.
why: Reference data is P3 rwb-case under the R-PREC default ruling and DP-07, and the client must not carry a list of its own; the values themselves are in TSD P10 v2 T3.2.
read: Template and Rules §R3 default ruling; DP-07; TSD P10 v2 T3.2; TSD P10 v2 T6.2
impact: A read at run time and one refusal path; no list literal in the service.

text: The legacy feature flag rwb.agent.client is kept as a data row of the platform feature-flag library under the R-PREC default ruling; off means no agent call, the rule result applied and a null agent version on the record.
why: Feature flags belong to the platform library under the default ruling, and the legacy exception path X6 depends on the flag as well as on the mode; the story must state where the flag lives.
read: Template and Rules §R3 default ruling; legacy sections 5 and 13
applied_in: RWB-P10-TE013-APP section 13; RWB-P10-TE013-OPS AC6 and section 4
impact: One flag row and one behaviour branch that the legacy story already defines.

text: The app slice reads the admin read through a gateway-bff pass-through stub and never calls rwb-agent directly; the exact route name and path in front of the read are fixed by the edge story and are not a deliverable of this story.
why: DP-19 makes the gateway-bff route the only entry for a screen, and no source names the route path of this read; the app story can be built and tested against a pass-through stub.
read: DP-19; ADR-019; Arch v5 slide 20; RWB-PLT-N001-CON
impact: The read is reachable through one hop and the route path is agreed once for every screen.

text: The fallback reason vocabulary keeps TIMED_OUT, SCHEMA and NO_POLICY with the legacy wording and adds MODEL_ERROR and TOOL_UNAVAILABLE for a model error and a consumed read that exceeds its budget, each mapping to a status of LOV-AGENT-RUN or to no run at all.
why: The legacy story names three reasons and the target has two boundary failures the legacy monolith did not have; the statuses must stay inside the list of TSD P10 v2 T3.2.
read: Legacy sections 5 and 12; TSD P10 v2 T3.2 LOV-AGENT-RUN; RWB-P10-E1058-CON AC5
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-agent and the data steward
impact: Two extra values in one vocabulary, both already in the list of values of the service.

text: The REST member names and types of AgentStepRequest, RuleResult and AgentStepOutcome are the ones this contract fixes from the legacy Java records, with JSON media type and the inputs reference as an opaque string; the exact form of the reference is settled with the data steward.
why: The legacy section 12 gives Java records and no serialization, and a REST contract cannot be tested without a media type and member names.
confirm: Solution architect and the data steward
impact: One shape per member, testable against the fakes; values are unchanged.

text: The local decision-record library returns a record reference and the step key is the lookup key of the record, so one step key has one record and a repeat returns the first reference; the link column stores that reference.
why: The legacy story fixes one entry per step key and the target writes the record through a library whose reference is not named by any source.
read: Legacy AC7 and section 12; DP-03; R-UNI-40; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON
confirm: Owner of the decision-record library and of P7 rwb-decision
impact: One lookup rule and one column; the repeat of AC7 stays one effect.

text: Each refusal of the run-step operation answers a platform status code and, where a business message applies, the legacy message ID: 403 with MSG-P4-002, 422 with MSG-GEN-001, 500 with MSG-P7-003, 409 for a repeat that returns the stored outcome, and 401, 404 and 503 without a business message.
why: The legacy section 12 names the errors 401, 403 and 503 of the admin read and the legacy section 14 gives two messages; the operation's own taxonomy has to be stated once.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-agent and the message-catalogue owner
impact: No new message text; the codes are the platform's.

text: The gateway-bff route in front of the run-step operation and the two reads is a pass-through of one hop, and its route name and path are fixed by the edge story; this contract fixes only the pass-through shape.
why: DP-19 makes the route the only entry for staff, and no source names the path; the contract and the deployment can be built and tested against a stub.
read: DP-19; ADR-019; Arch v5 slide 20; RWB-PLT-N001-CON
applied_in: RWB-P10-TE013-CON AC5 and section 12.8; RWB-P10-TE013-OPS AC7 and section 15
impact: One route for three operations, agreed once for every screen.

text: The fallback sweep that replaces the legacy Quartz entry is registered as the Schedule AgentStepFallbackSweep in namespace rwb-recovery on the task queue rwb-agent.
why: DP-10 replaces the shared scheduler with a Schedule or an event-started workflow in the owning service, and no source names the sweep of this key.
read: DP-10; ADR-016; Arch v5 slides 16 and 44; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON
confirm: DevOps lead and the platform administrator of the namespace
impact: One Schedule registration; a rename is a registration change with no code change.

text: The sweep reads rwb.agent.events.v1 under its own consumer group, named rwb-agent-step, to reconcile the fallback facts of a business date against the rows of rwb_agent; it reads no topic of another service.
why: The release needs a consumer group for the reconciliation read and no source names one; the business consumers of the topic hold their own groups.
confirm: Platform administrator of the Kafka platform
impact: One group on one topic; no effect on the groups of rwb-decision, rwb-document or rwb-deviation.

text: The deployment topology detail - cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class, probe timings - and the host, the SKU and the budget are values of the environment and not story decisions; the chart exposes them and hard-codes none.
why: No source fixes a cluster, a replica count or a budget, and the platform epics own the topology; the story fixes only their names and the rule that they are values.
read: Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; Arch v5 slide 45; RWB-PLT-TPL
confirm: Release manager and the platform team
impact: Environment values only; no behaviour changes.

text: The fallback sweep runs daily at 02:30 Asia/Bangkok for the previous business date, with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window of one business date, and a manual start for any business date joins the same workflow identity.
why: The sweep replaces a legacy job whose time no source states for this key, and DP-10 requires a cadence, an overlap policy and a catch-up window to be declared.
read: DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44 (Schedule conventions); RWB-PLT-E1071-CON
confirm: DevOps lead and the on-call rota
impact: One cadence; a change is a registration change.

text: The host, port, certificate and Key Vault entries of the Enterprise AI private endpoint INT-23 are the infrastructure story's; this deployment only opens the private route from the rwb-agent namespace to the endpoint the agent platform uses and opens no other outside route.
why: TSD P10 v2 T5.1 names INT-23 and no endpoint detail, and Arch v5 slide 16 puts the call inside the service's platform; the deployment must still state its egress.
read: TSD P10 v2 T5.1; Arch v5 slide 16; RWB-P10-E1058-CON; RWB-P10-E1058-INF
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure and the security administrator
impact: One egress rule and no credential in the chart.
